title: First prenatal visit
typical: Usually booked for after about week 8; the sources say to call as soon as you think you are pregnant.
note: Providers usually do not book it before about week 8, but an earlier visit is common when there is a medical condition, a past pregnancy problem, or symptoms such as bleeding.

sources.name: NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)
MedlinePlus: Prenatal Care
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your first trimester

title: Prenatal visits about once a month
typical: About one visit a month until week 28 in a healthy pregnancy.
note: People over 35 or with conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure may be seen more often, and each practice sets its own schedule.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Prenatal Care
NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your first trimester

title: Prenatal visits every 2 weeks
typical: About every 2 weeks from week 28 to week 36 in a healthy pregnancy.
note: Higher-risk pregnancies can mean more frequent visits and extra monitoring, and the exact rhythm depends on the practice.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Prenatal Care
NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your third trimester

title: Weekly prenatal visits until birth
typical: About once a week from week 36 until the baby is born in a healthy pregnancy.
note: The third-trimester page notes extra tests and fetal monitoring may be ordered for high-risk pregnancies or one that runs past 40 weeks.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Prenatal Care
NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your third trimester

title: First-visit blood and urine tests
typical: Done at the first prenatal visit: blood type and Rh, blood count, rubella immunity, hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis and a urine check.
note: The list is consistent across the sources but the exact panel differs by practice, and extra tests may be offered based on age, history or family background.

sources.name: NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your first trimester
MedlinePlus: Prenatal Testing

title: Cell-free DNA blood screening
typical: Can be done from about week 10; the sources give no upper limit.
note: It is recommended for higher-risk pregnancies such as age 35 or older, and many providers also offer it to everyone.

sources.name: MedlinePlus: Prenatal Cell-Free DNA Screening
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your first trimester

title: Mid-pregnancy anatomy ultrasound
typical: Usually between weeks 18 and 22.
note: The range comes from an NIH-hosted reference plus an NHS cross-check (18 to 21), not from ACOG, and a higher-risk pregnancy may get extra or earlier scans.

sources.name: StatPearls on NCBI Bookshelf (NIH-hosted reference, not a guideline body): Sonography Fetal Assessment, Protocols, and Interpretation
NHS (UK) Screening tests in pregnancy [CROSS-CHECK ONLY, not a US source]

title: Gestational diabetes glucose screening
typical: Usually between weeks 24 and 28.
note: CDC says people at higher risk of gestational diabetes may be tested earlier.

sources.name: CDC: Diabetes Testing
NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)

title: Group B strep (GBS) swab
typical: During the 36th or 37th week of each pregnancy.
note: CDC says screening still applies when a cesarean birth is planned, and the third-trimester page only says "a few weeks before your due date".

sources.name: CDC: Screening for Group B Strep Bacteria
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Prenatal care in your third trimester

title: Tdap (whooping cough) vaccine in pregnancy
typical: One dose in every pregnancy, best given between weeks 27 and 36, earlier in that window if possible.
note: It may be given at any point in pregnancy, and CDC says to give it right after birth if it was missed.

sources.name: CDC: Vaccine Recommendations Before, During, and After Pregnancy
CDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women (clinician page)
NICHD: What happens during prenatal visits? (page review date is 2017, so older than the others)

title: Flu shot in pregnancy (season-based, not week-based)
typical: Any week of pregnancy during flu season; CDC says ideally by the end of October.
note: Timing follows the season, not the week of pregnancy: September or October is preferred in the first two trimesters, and July or August can be considered in the third.

sources.name: CDC: Vaccine Recommendations Before, During, and After Pregnancy
CDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women (clinician page)

title: RSV vaccine in pregnancy
typical: One dose between 32 weeks 0 days and 36 weeks 6 days, September through January in most of the continental US.
note: If the window is missed or the pregnant parent is not vaccinated, the baby can get an RSV antibody instead, and regions outside the continental US follow local guidance.

sources.name: CDC: RSV Vaccine Guidance for Pregnant Women (page shows two unlabeled dates, 2024-08-30 and 2025-01-31)
CDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women (clinician page)
CDC: Vaccine Recommendations Before, During, and After Pregnancy

title: Newborn screening heel-prick blood spot
typical: Done before the baby leaves the hospital, usually when the baby is 1 to 2 days old.
note: The fetched pages say only "before leaving the hospital" or "shortly after birth", and the 1 to 2 day figure comes from search results of HRSA and CDC documents, which also say a test before 24 hours may need repeating.

title: Newborn hearing screen
typical: Ideally before leaving the hospital, and no later than 1 month old.
note: CDC's 1-3-6 guideline adds a full hearing evaluation by 3 months and early intervention by 6 months for babies who do not pass, and the sources give no separate timing for babies with risk factors.

title: First pediatric visit (first-week visit)
typical: AAP lists a first-week visit when the baby is 3 to 5 days old.
note: The AAP page gives the age only, and the sources reviewed describe no high-risk or practice-level variations.

sources.name: AAP via HealthyChildren.org: AAP Schedule of Well-Child Care Visits

title: 1-month well-child visit
typical: AAP lists a well-child visit at 1 month.
note: The AAP page gives the age only, so exact booking and any extra visits are decided by the practice.

title: 2-month well-child visit
typical: AAP lists a well-child visit at 2 months; the first routine vaccine series is also given around this age.
note: The AAP page gives the age only, so exact booking and any extra visits are decided by the practice.

note: The AAP page gives the age only, so exact booking and any extra visits are decided by the practice.

note: The AAP page gives the age only, so exact booking and any extra visits are decided by the practice.

title: Early postpartum check-in (phone or in person)
typical: ACOG recommends contact with the care provider within the first 3 weeks after birth.
note: This comes from search-result snippets of ACOG Committee Opinion 736 because the ACOG site returned 402, and the sources reviewed give no separate high-risk timing.

sources.name: ACOG Committee Opinion 736, Optimizing Postpartum Care (PubMed record) [SEEN IN SEARCH RESULTS ONLY: ACOG site returned 402, PubMed fetch blocked]

title: Comprehensive postpartum visit
typical: ACOG says no later than 12 weeks after birth, while older MedlinePlus text still says a single checkup at 4 to 6 weeks.
note: The sources disagree on a single 4 to 6 week visit versus a 3-week contact plus a visit by 12 weeks, and both were seen only in search results, so confirm with ACOG.

sources.name: ACOG Committee Opinion 736, Optimizing Postpartum Care (PubMed record) [SEEN IN SEARCH RESULTS ONLY: ACOG site returned 402, PubMed fetch blocked]
MedlinePlus Encyclopedia: Vaginal delivery - discharge (says 4 to 6 weeks) [SEEN IN SEARCH RESULTS ONLY, page not fetched]

title: Safe sleep space: firm flat crib or bassinet in your room
typical: AAP says to share a room, not a bed, for at least the first 6 months, with the baby on their back on a firm, flat surface.
note: AAP gives no deadline for setting up the sleep space before the baby comes home, and most of the advice applies to babies up to 1 year old.

sources.name: AAP via HealthyChildren.org: A Parent's Guide to Safe Sleep
